key_insight: A 3D COMSOL opto-electro-thermal model shows that n-ZnSe/p-SrScCu3Se4/p+-WSe2 can achieve high photovoltaic efficiency when absorber width, doping, and defect levels are optimized.
engineering_relevance: The study identifies SrScCu3Se4 as a promising quaternary chalcogenide absorber for designing high-performance, thermally aware solar-cell architectures.
method: Self-consistent coupling of optical generation, drift-diffusion transport, and thermal loss
Parameter sweep of absorber width, acceptor density, and bulk defects
evidence_signal: Under optimized conditions, the device reached VOC = 1.02 V, JSC = 32.472 mA/cm2, FF = 88.212%, and PCE = 29.217%, with QE strongest in the visible spectrum.
watch_item: Performance may be sensitive to near-infrared absorption losses and spatially non-uniform heating, so experimental validation and thermal management are important before fabrication.
paper_title: Computational analysis and performance optimization of SrScCu3Se4-based solar cells using COMSOL Multiphysics
